## Paper

The Logic of Collective Action

## World

public_goods

## Institution

No-institution collective-action baseline.

## Agent type

Self-interested group members / learning agents.

## Theoretical benchmark

Group benefit does not guarantee individual contribution; free-rider incentives dominate absent institutions.

## Learning setup

Repeated public-goods/commons interaction with private reward incentives.

## Metrics

Contribution, extraction, sustainability, welfare, group outcome versus individual incentive.

## Main result

Individuals in large groups do not act to achieve common interests due to free-rider problem; small groups may show some voluntary cooperation but it is often suboptimal

## What they prove

Do not cite this extracted card for a detailed proof without checking the original chapter. In this repo, the source is used for the collective-action benchmark that shared group benefit does not by itself eliminate individual free-rider incentives.

## What they only simulate

Not applicable for this card's thesis use: it is a collective-action theory anchor, not a simulation benchmark.

## What they do NOT test

Learning agents, dynamic pool regeneration, artificial reward-shaping institutions, and cross-world capability ladders.

## What we need to reproduce

Explain why low contribution is expected under private incentives and do not treat it as a bug without checking incentives.

## How our project differs

The book is broad collective-action theory. This repo operationalizes one narrow dynamic public-pool version for learning agents.

## Implementation obligations

Private payoff mapping; public benefit mapping; contribution/extraction metrics; institution comparisons against baseline.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

baseline extraction/contribution/sustainability metrics; outputs/public_goods_full.

## Failure modes to audit

Assuming agents should contribute because welfare would improve; no individual payoff explanation; interpreting low contribution as failed learning only.

## Project code comparison

Compare The Logic of Collective Action to Public Goods baseline behavior. The repo should use it to justify the expected commons pressure before judging institutions.
